content:
Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness device similar to the WHOOP or Fitbit Air. As someone who has been using WHOOP for the past 6 months, I do think this concept is good, but there are a few areas where I hope Apple can do better.

As for what Apple's screenless fitness device will look like, we don't have many details for now, because the product is still in the early stages of development and won't be launched until 2028 at the earliest. Bloomberg described it as 'a slim fabric wristband with a built-in sensor module'.

Earlier this year, WHOOP and Chase launched a promotional campaign where Chase Sapphire credit card users could get a WHOOP at a discounted price or for free, so I took the opportunity to apply. I've been using WHOOP since, but I've never fully committed to using it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection is never perfect, and I find it annoying to have to specifically take out my phone to log a workout, whether before or after the activity. With Apple Watch, you can start a workout directly on the watch face, while WHOOP syncs the time back from Apple Health. This is the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

In the gym, taking out my phone might be more acceptable, but when I go cycling or hiking, I don't want the hassle of dealing with my phone.

So, for Apple's screenless fitness device, I really hope to see a button and indicator light for starting and stopping workouts. You'd still need to go to your phone to categorise the workout, but I'd rather do that later than in the moment. Apple could also develop a categorisation model based on certain factors.

Summary

If Apple can really develop a screenless fitness device that's useful without having to take out your phone, I think it would be quite appealing. This form factor has many benefits, including comfortable wear, longer battery life, and the ability to be worn alongside a traditional watch.

TB's Hot Comments

I bought the FitBit Air because after wearing Apple Watch for so many years, I started to get a bit tired of it. I like mechanical watches, but I also want to keep tracking my health data and enjoy the convenience a watch brings, like being able to use Apple Pay without taking out my phone, or using it to open doors when my hands are full. If Apple can come out with a product that integrates perfectly with their ecosystem, supports a streamlined version of Apple Pay, door keys, car keys, and other NFC functions, plus can connect to AirPods to have Siri read me notifications or perform actions, I'll definitely buy it the first chance I get.

Personally speaking, after trying WHOOP, I'm sure I prefer smartwatches, even if the battery life is shorter. I understand some people want a screenless device to reduce distractions, but for me, I just turn on the 'Do Not Disturb' mode on my watch and that does the job.

What do you think about Apple developing a screenless fitness device? How much would you be willing to pay? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
